original_query: with customer_total_return as  (select wr_returning_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk  ,ca_state as ctr_state ,wr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(wr_return_amt) as ctr_total_return  from web_returns      ,date_dim      ,customer_address      ,item  where wr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk    and d_year =1998    and wr_returning_addr_sk = ca_address_sk    and wr_item_sk = i_item_sk    and i_manager_id BETWEEN 40 and 49    and wr_return_amt / wr_return_quantity between 3 and 32  group by wr_returning_customer_sk          ,ca_state, wr_reason_sk)   select  c_customer_id,c_salutation,c_first_name,c_last_name,c_preferred_cust_flag        ,c_birth_day,c_birth_month,c_birth_year,c_birth_country,c_login,c_email_address        ,c_last_review_date_sk,ctr_total_return  from customer_total_return ctr1      ,customer_address      ,customer  where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2  			  from customer_total_return ctr2                   	  where ctr1.ctr_state = ctr2.ctr_state)        and ca_address_sk = c_current_addr_sk        and ca_state in ('IN', 'KS', 'NE', 'VA')        and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk        and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk in (11, 18)       and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1937 AND 1943  order by c_customer_id,c_salutation,c_first_name,c_last_name,c_preferred_cust_flag                   ,c_birth_day,c_birth_month,c_birth_year,c_birth_country,c_login,c_email_address                   ,c_last_review_date_sk,ctr_total_return limit 100;
rewritten_query:
with customer_total_return as (
    select wr.wr_returning_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk
          ,ra.ca_state as ctr_state
          ,wr.wr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk
          ,sum(wr.wr_return_amt) as ctr_total_return
    from web_returns wr
    join date_dim d on wr.wr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    join customer_address ra on wr.wr_returning_addr_sk = ra.ca_address_sk
    join item i on wr.wr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    where d.d_year = 1998
      and i.i_manager_id between 40 and 49
      and wr.wr_return_amt / wr.wr_return_quantity between 3 and 32
    group by wr.wr_returning_customer_sk, ra.ca_state, wr.wr_reason_sk
),
state_avg as (
    select ctr_state
          ,avg(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 as ctr_avg_threshold
    from customer_total_return
    group by ctr_state
)
select c.c_customer_id
      ,c.c_salutation
      ,c.c_first_name
      ,c.c_last_name
      ,c.c_preferred_cust_flag
      ,c.c_birth_day
      ,c.c_birth_month
      ,c.c_birth_year
      ,c.c_birth_country
      ,c.c_login
      ,c.c_email_address
      ,c.c_last_review_date_sk
      ,ctr1.ctr_total_return
from customer_total_return ctr1
join state_avg sa
  on ctr1.ctr_state = sa.ctr_state
 and ctr1.ctr_total_return > sa.ctr_avg_threshold
join customer c
  on ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
join customer_address ca
  on ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
where ctr1.ctr_reason_sk in (11, 18)
  and ca.ca_state in ('IN', 'KS', 'NE', 'VA')
  and c.c_birth_year between 1937 and 1943
order by c.c_customer_id
        ,c.c_salutation
        ,c.c_first_name
        ,c.c_last_name
        ,c.c_preferred_cust_flag
        ,c.c_birth_day
        ,c.c_birth_month
        ,c.c_birth_year
        ,c.c_birth_country
        ,c.c_login
        ,c.c_email_address
        ,c.c_last_review_date_sk
        ,ctr1.ctr_total_return
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated subquery computing avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 per state with a pre-aggregated state_avg CTE and join it back on ctr_state. This eliminates the per-row subplan scan of customer_total_return.
Convert the implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOIN syntax in both the CTE and the outer query, improving readability and enabling clearer join-order optimization by the planner.

Keep the ctr_reason_sk IN (11,18) filter in the outer query (not inside the CTE) because the state average must be computed over all reasons to preserve original semantics; the filter reduces rows before joining customer and customer_address.
Push the c_birth_year and ca_state filters onto the respective base tables (customer, customer_address) via explicit joins so the planner can apply them early during table scans.
Constants (d_year = 1998, i_manager_id range, birth-year range, reason list) remain literal in the query so the optimizer can fold them and use them for partition pruning/index scans.
